class.name: MidiIn
class.brief_description: Receives MIDI input from hardware and software MIDI ports.
class.description:
[MidiIn] provides real-time MIDI input functionality using RtMidi. It allows you to open physical MIDI ports or create virtual MIDI ports to receive MIDI messages from controllers, keyboards, and other MIDI devices.
By default, MIDI messages are received through the [signal midi_message] signal. To poll for messages instead (for example in [method Node._process]), set [member use_signals] to [code]false[/code] and call [method get_message] until it returns an empty array.
Use the static methods [method get_port_names] and [method get_port_count] to discover available MIDI input ports before opening a connection.

method.name: open_port
method.description: Opens a MIDI input port by its index number. Port indices are zero-based and can be determined using [method get_port_names] or [method get_port_count]. Returns [constant OK] on success, [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] if [param port_number] doesn't exist, [constant ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE] if a port is already open, [constant ERR_CANT_OPEN] if no ports are available or the port could not be opened, or [constant ERR_UNAVAILABLE] if MIDI input could not be initialized. On Android, opening ports needs the addon's Android library in the app: enable the godot_rtmidi editor plugin and [b]Use Gradle Build[/b] in the Android export preset (see the README). Without it, this returns [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED]. [codeblock] var err = midi_in.open_port(0) if err != OK: print("Could not open MIDI input: ", error_string(err)) [/codeblock]

method.name: open_virtual_port
method.description: Creates and opens a virtual MIDI input port with the specified name. This allows other applications to connect to this port and send MIDI messages. The port name is displayed in MIDI port lists of other applications. Virtual ports are supported on macOS, iOS, Linux and Windows. On Android and other platforms this returns [constant ERR_UNAVAILABLE]. On Windows, virtual ports use Windows MIDI Services and need Windows 11 25H2 or later with its API ([code]Windows.Devices.Midi2[/code], installed by Windows Update) and the 64-bit build. Otherwise this returns [constant ERR_UNAVAILABLE]; create a virtual port with a loopback driver such as loopMIDI and open it with [method open_port] instead. Other applications see this port as a MIDI output. The first call can take a few seconds while Windows starts its MIDI service. On iOS, the app must declare the [code]audio[/code] background mode, or this returns [constant ERR_CANT_OPEN]. Add [code]<key>UIBackgroundModes</key><array><string>audio</string></array>[/code] to [b]Additional Plist Content[/b] in the iOS export preset. Returns [constant OK] on success, [constant ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE] if a port is already open, [constant ERR_CANT_OPEN] if the port could not be created, or [constant ERR_TIMEOUT] if the Windows MIDI service did not answer.

method.name: close_port
method.description: Closes the open MIDI input port, regular or virtual. After closing, you must open another port before receiving MIDI messages again. Returns [constant OK], or [constant ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] without printing an error if no port was open.

method.name: is_port_open
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if a MIDI input port, regular or virtual, is currently open, [code]false[/code] otherwise.

method.name: get_port_count
method.description: Returns the number of available MIDI input ports on the system.

method.name: get_port_name
method.description: Returns the name of the MIDI input port at the specified index. Returns an empty string if the port index is invalid.

method.name: get_port_names
method.description: Returns an array containing the names of all available MIDI input ports on the system.

method.name: ignore_types
method.description: Configures which types of MIDI messages to ignore. By default, system exclusive (sysex), timing clock, and active sensing messages are ignored to reduce message overhead. Set parameters to [code]false[/code] to receive these message types.

method.name: get_message
set_buffer_size
method.description: Sets the internal MIDI message buffer size. [param buffer_size] is the size of each buffer in bytes, and [param buffer_count] is the number of buffers to allocate. Larger buffers reduce the chance of message loss on high-volume MIDI input, but use more memory.

method.name: show_bluetooth_devices
method.description: Shows the system's list of Bluetooth MIDI devices, where the user can connect or disconnect devices. A connected device then shows up in [method MidiIn.get_port_names] and [method MidiOut.get_port_names] like any other port, in this and every other app, until it is disconnected. On iOS, the list closes when the user taps [b]Done[/b]. Check the port list again afterwards. This is available on iOS and Android, where an app has to connect Bluetooth MIDI devices itself. On other platforms it returns [constant ERR_UNAVAILABLE]; on macOS, connect Bluetooth MIDI devices in Audio MIDI Setup instead. [b]Android:[/b] shows the system's companion device picker, filtered to Bluetooth LE MIDI devices; no Bluetooth or location permission is needed. The chosen device is connected and stays connected until the app exits. Needs the addon's Android library (enable the godot_rtmidi editor plugin and [b]Use Gradle Build[/b]), otherwise this returns [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED]. The method returns as soon as the picker is shown; the device's ports appear a moment after the user picks it. Computers that support both classic Bluetooth and Bluetooth LE (e.g. a Mac sharing MIDI over Bluetooth) may disconnect right away, because Android connects to them over classic Bluetooth. [b]iOS:[/b] the app must declare why it uses Bluetooth, or iOS terminates it. Add [code]<key>NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription</key><string>Connects to Bluetooth MIDI devices.</string>[/code] to [b]Additional Plist Content[/b] in the iOS export preset. Without it, this method returns [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED] instead of showing the list. Returns [constant OK] when the list is shown, or [constant ERR_BUSY] if it is already showing. [codeblock] func _on_bluetooth_button_pressed(): var err := MidiIn.show_bluetooth_devices() if err != OK: print("Can't show Bluetooth MIDI devices: ", error_string(err)) [/codeblock]

members.member: If [code]true[/code], incoming messages are emitted through [signal midi_message]. If [code]false[/code], they are queued and must be read with [method get_message]. Messages arriving while signals are used are not queued.

signal.name: midi_message
signal.description: Emitted when a MIDI message is received. [param deltatime] is the time in seconds since the last message, and [param message] is the MIDI message data as a byte array.

signal.name: midi_error
signal.description: Emitted when RtMidi reports an error or warning. [param error_type] is one of the [enum MidiError] constants, and [param error_message] is a human-readable error description. If nothing is connected to this signal, the error is printed to the console instead. Once you connect to it, handling the error is up to you. Errors caused by invalid method arguments are always printed and reported through return values, not this signal.
